newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-CZECHS LICK WOUNDS AFTER BITTER PENALTY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CZECHS LICK WOUNDS AFTER BITTER PENALTY.

text.p: The Czech Republic could do little but console itself on Monday as it digested the depth of its fall from the heady heights of the Euro 96 finals to also-rans, knocked out of the 1998 World Cup after only five qualifiers.
Less than a year ago, the Czech Republic stunned the soccer world by taking Germany to the limit in the European championship final.
On Sunday night, the Czechs attacked with a vengeance early but could not muster up the goal needed against Group 6 leaders Spain.
Instead, they saw their dim chances of qualifying for France fade into the Spanish night with a questionable penalty call on keeper Pavel Srnicek leading to the game's only goal.
"Good-bye France, the Czechs are not coming! We were kept out by an actor!" blared the headline of the tabloid daily Blesk in Prague.
Added the leading sports daily Sport: "A bitter end after an unjust penalty."

With only four points from five games, the beaten Euro 96 finalists have no chance of qualifying, and face the further humiliation of finishing behind the lowly Faroe Islands, perched ahead of the Czechs with six points from seven games.
Spain lead group six with 16 points, while Yugoslavia are on 15 points from six matches and Slovakia third on 12 points. Only the top team in each group is guaranteed a spot in the World Cup.
"I am so sad. To be second in Europe and then not be able to fight at the World Cup is very troubling," said Czech football union head Frantisek Chvalovsky.
He quickly moved, however, to dispel any rumour that coach Dusan Uhrin would be fired, saying the coach had his full support.

As has been the case since losing to Germany in the Euro final at Wembley, the Czechs failed to find the scoring touch that led to highlights such as Karel Poborsky's cheeky chip shot to beat Portugal in the quarterfinals.
In five games, the Czechs have scored only seven goals, six of which came from a 6-0 win over lowly Malta.
"When we don't score goals, there is not much you can do. And that has been the story for us throughout the qualifying," said Newcastle United goalkeeper Srnicek.
